laws.rule: Hol Chan Marine Reserve (off Ambergris Caye, run by the Belize Fisheries Department with the reserve's management team) bans, reserve-wide: removing or disturbing plants, animals, rocks, corals, shells or sand without the fisheries administrator's authorisation; discharging waste, toxic material or litter; long lines, fish traps, seine nets, gill nets and spearfishing; and anchoring that may damage coral or sensitive habitat. Fishing of any kind needs a valid licence.

At Hol Chan, snorkelling and diving in the recreational zones requires registration, and scuba diving requires certification or a course led by a certified instructor. In Zone A (Hol Chan Channel) and Zone H (Mexico Rocks no-take zone) only fins and a mask are allowed, with no gloves, no fishing and no feeding fish. In Zone D (Shark Ray Alley) there's no scuba diving, no gloves and no harassing animals; guides may feed sharks from the boat. Tour boats must be registered with a visible sticker and check in with the ranger, may not exceed 45 feet or carry more than 30 people, must fly a divers-down flag, use moorings, stay no more than 1 hour in the exclusive recreational area and take no more than 8 people per guide. The page describes some zones only in part.

A State of Emergency declared by the Government of Belize covers designated areas of Belize City and parts of Ladyville, in this district. Smartraveller says to expect more police and possible disruptions, and to follow local authorities. Check local media for the current areas.

local-law.notes: Only Hol Chan is covered for Belize District. Blue Hole Natural Monument rules, Belize City and Caye Caulker rules, and district-level alcohol or beach rules aren't checked.

layers.authority: Hol Chan Marine Reserve, Belize Fisheries Department
layers.process: The Fisheries Department's reserve page states one fee: sport fishing in Zone E (Bajos) costs BZ$20 per person per day (about A$14.20 at A$1 = USD 0.7040, RBA 30 October 2026, and BZ$2 = USD 1, the fixed peg). It doesn't list a reserve entry fee for snorkellers and divers. A local newspaper reported a US$15 entry fee for all zones from 1 August 2024 (about A$21.31), with the local rate unchanged for Belizeans showing ID; that report is a signal, not an official notice, and conflicts with itself on a US$20 figure. Many tour operators include the fee in the tour price. Confirm with the reserve office on +501-226-2247.
